subject: MSA: proposed inspection bands, pen-test handback, and evidence tempo
messages:
From: Claire Monroe <claire@healthsync.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>; Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-06-17 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA security exhibit — proposed inspection bands and evidence tempo

Irene / Marissa —

Thanks again for walking us through the platform last week. Procurement asked me to surface a couple of operational details so they can complete the security review and confirmation of the order form:

1) Pen-test window: we'd like to propose a 72-hour window for active testing and a 14-day notice requirement. Can Redwood confirm whether ephemeral/ephemeral-staging access will be available for the tester, and whether the platform can provide filtered logs for the 72-hour window (read-only export)?

2) Inspection bands & sampling: our security team wants the MSA exhibit to call out bounded inspection bands (e.g., tenant-scoped ephemeral inspection vs. full on-prem inspection). Can you provide suggested language and an evidence cadence we'd need to expect (weekly artifact pulls vs. one-off handbacks)?

3) Evidence handback: what format(s) do you provide for SOC 2 evidence packages (CSV manifest, supported exports) and can Redwood commit to a 30-day turnaround on ad-hoc evidence requests?

Attached: our draft order form and a short pen-test window proposal so you can redline.

Looking for a short call early next week if needed — procurement is aiming to sign by end of month.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Monroe
Head of Security Partnerships | HealthSync
claire@healthsync.com
Attachments: HealthSync-orderform-draft.pdf, pen-test-window-proposal.pdf
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: MSA security exhibit — proposed inspection bands and evidence tempo

Claire —

Appreciate the clear ask list. Short answers up front, then proposed next steps: 

- Pen-test window: Redwood supports ephemeral staging pools and can grant scoped test access for a bounded window. We typically require a minimum 7-day notice to schedule, but for partners we can accept 14-day notice and agree to a 72-hour active testing window. We can provide filtered logs and a read-only export. I will flag the export retention window with infra (usually 90 days; can be extended per order form).

- Inspection bands: we propose three bands in the security exhibit: "Tenant-limited" (no customer data), "Tenant-scoped with sampling" (limited datasets, auditor IAM), and "Privileged inspection" (for on-prem/VPC with legal-approved scope). I attached suggested exhibit wording in docx for your redline.

- Evidence handback: SOC 2 artifact packages are delivered as ZIPs with a CSV manifest; ad-hoc evidence requests we aim to fulfill within 30 business days by default. For deal-level SLAs (e.g., 30 calendar days), we'll surface that in the order form and lock to a committed response SLA for enterprise customers.

Next steps: Marissa, Karthik — can you review the attached redline and advise on (1) whether legal is comfortable with the three-band model and (2) whether we should accept HealthSync's 30-day calendar turnaround or counter to 30 business days? If legal needs an internal signoff, propose we do a 30-minute sync Thu morning.

Claire — if you'd rather avoid a call, we're happy to put a tracked Word doc next to the order form and iterate.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
Irene.Choi@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2025-06-18 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA security exhibit — proposed inspection bands and evidence tempo

Quick legal summary —

I reviewed the suggested exhibit wording and propose the following edits (high level):

- Define "inspection band" explicitly and map to contractual artifacts (e.g., Tenant-limited -> exported logs & config snapshots; Privileged -> controlled access with JIT and scoped non-prod environments).
- For pen-test windows, accept 72-hour active testing but require a pre-test scope signoff (test plan + IP ranges) and a post-test debrief within 5 business days. This reduces operational risk.
- Evidence SLA: counter to 30 calendar days with 30 business days for ad-hoc requests; accept 30 calendar days for pre-negotiated "assurance addendum" on enterprise order forms.
- Add a standard redaction clause for customer-submitted evidence to protect third-party PII and internal logs.

I've inserted inline redlines in HealthSync-MSA-redlines-v1.docx and added a short penalty/credit line for SLA miss of evidence turnovers (sample language only).

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Attachments: HealthSync-MSA-redlines-v1.docx (with inline comments)

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the detailed redlines. A few clarifications from procurement and scheduling: 

1) HealthSync is OK with the 30 business day default for ad-hoc evidence requests if Redwood will commit in the order form to a 30 calendar day SLA if we purchase the assurance addendum. Please insert the assurance addendum reference in section 7.2 and we'll route for signature.

2) For pen-tests: we'll send the test-plan + IP ranges 10 business days prior. Can you confirm JIT elevation timeline (how quickly can Redwood grant scoped test IAM for ephemeral staging)? We need guaranteed access within 24 hours of acceptance to meet our external vendor schedule.

3) DocuSign & redlines: procurement prefers tracked Word comments rather than multiple calls. Please upload the redlined docx to the Drive link you provided and share a DocuSign-ready order form link when legal and security are aligned.

If you can make the two small counters above, we should be able to route this to signing by next week.
